newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief asks if policy should focus on Internet.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief asks if policy should focus on Internet.

text.p: The nation's top communications regulator raised the question Thursday of whether government policy should begin focusing on the smooth and reliabile operation of the Internet computer network.

"One of the things we'd like to find out is whether or not reliability is in fact an appropriate policy issue with respect to the packet-switched network," Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt told industry officials at the start of an FCC forum on "bandwidth."

"Or would you say to us, no, that is not of any particular importance, and if I happen to rely on packet-switched technology to get my sports, news, or make stock market trades, well it's not terribily important if that doesn't work for several hours or days."
A packet-switched network refers to the type of network over which the Internet operates.

The FCC convened the meeting of industry officials -- who shared their views with the agency -- at a time when the local phone and Internet industries are debating whether traffic in cyberspace is clogging the nation's local phone network.

A coalition of Internet and computer companies on Wednesday said in a study that the growing mass of Internet users have paid their fair share to local phone cmopanies and pose little threat to the phone system.
Local carriers have issued their own studies seeking to justify new acess fees on Internet usage, saying such usage threatens to overwhelm the phone system.
The FCC already focuses on ensuring the reliability of the phone network so that in the event of a crisis -- such as a hurricane or a flood -- there is adequate capacity to ensure continuous service.
Late last year Hundt urged a high-level industry advisory group -- the Network Reliability Council -- to keep an eye on the impact of surging Internet use on the local phone network.

In his remarks Thursday, Hundt asked whether ensuring the reliability of the Internet also should be a mission of the council -- just like the group now seeks to ensure the reliability of the traditional phone network.
"Or in fact should it be the case that it isn't as important that the Internet be reliabile in the same way as the circuit-switched network," Hundt added.
